text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Opposition MPs said they had the required 10 votes to call for a no-confidence motion on Finance Minister Nasser al-Rodhan but decided not to take the issue to that point. The minister was grilled in parliament on Tuesday over alleged irregularities in key financial bodies which he heads.
- Movie, music agents say piracy still rampant. Kuwait introduced two years ago legal protection for U.S. and British movie and music products but a comprehensive copyright law has yet to be issued.

- Jordanian Prime Minister Abdul Salam al-Majali hopes his country will normalise ties with Kuwait which downgraded relations with several states for siding with former occupier Iraq during the 1990-91 Gulf crisis.

- Most Jordanians still harbour feelings of enmity towards Kuwait, the head of parliament's foreign affairs committee says. Kuwait MP Abdul-Aziz al-Adasani urged his country to slow down moves to improve ties with states which backed Iraq.
- MP Adasani says positive statements from Sudan indicate a wish to improve ties with Kuwait.
- General Binford Peay, head of U.S. forces in the Gulf, reiterates his country's commitment to the security of Kuwait. Peay arrived in Kuwait on Tuesday from Saudi Arabia.
- Kuwait wins first gold medal at Pan Arab Games.
